ALPHABET CENTER · LETTER W

Letter W — Watermelon.

A striped watermelon rolls in for the letter W. W is the longest letter to say — double-u — and one zigzag stroke to write: down, up, down, up.

Meet the letter, hear its sound, trace it together — then play. Everything on this page is free, gentle and paced for you.

THE LETTER SOUND

What does W say?

“w — wuh, a windy round sound”

W says wuh — made with rounded lips blowing gently, like blowing out a candle without blowing it out. Say wuh and feel your lips make a small circle.

TRACE THE LETTER

Trace W w together.

Follow the numbers with a finger — on screen or on each other’s palms. The arrows show the way to go, the numbers show where to start, and a grown-up reads the little script below each card. Slow and wobbly is exactly right.

Trace the uppercase W

One stroke. Start at 1 at the top left: slide down, up, down, up — four straight lines, no lift.

Trace the lowercase w

One stroke. Start at 1 at the top left: slide down, up, down, up — four straight lines, no lift.

TAKE IT OFF SCREEN

Watermelon picnic.

Two minutes is plenty. Follow your child’s lead and stop while it is still fun — that is the whole method.

  1. 01

    Spread a towel and have a watermelon picnic (real or pretend).

  2. 02

    Knock on the watermelon with one knuckle — hear the wuh-wuh.

  3. 03

    Eat a slice with tiny bites, saying wuh between each one.

PLAY & PRACTICE

Games that use this letter.

The games mix every letter — play them after meeting two or three letters, or any day your child asks. No scores, no timers, no wrong answers that count.
